summary: Repaired and persisted the node1 status service. It now runs as statusd, serves the preserved document only for STATUS\n, returns ERROR for other requests, and restricts access to statusd/status-readers. The outsider account is denied. All behavior survived a verified node reboot without changing Ubuntu 24.04 or kernel 6.8.0-71-generic.
actions_performed: Created statusd, status-reader, outsider, and status-readers identities.
Repaired server.py and installed an enabled systemd service.
Applied 2750 statusd:status-readers permissions to run/ and 0660 to status.sock.
Preserved the status document with SHA-256 5b47f32d92c3ae9661d765212aa884f1610132293932355cfac4dc28b94f305b.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified full recovery.

evidence.summary: Account memberships show statusd and status-reader authorized through status-readers, while outsider has no authorized membership.

evidence.requirement: STATUS returns the supplied document; other requests return an error
evidence.summary: Both authorized identities received an exact document match; OTHER returned ERROR before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Service is available only to statusd and status-readers
evidence.summary: Socket is 0660 statusd:status-readers; outsider socket and document access were directly denied.
The document SHA-256 remained unchanged through repair and reboot.

Captured healthy baseline boot bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49, acknowledged the safe reboot, observed changed boot 89562349-005f-4212-9c90-06a6aaf05b0a, and proved recovered service, data, permissions, protocol behavior, and access isolation.
